items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: I know you and Piku, Rie Lee Barnes, George Lewis, all play that one special little part, you know, that chorus.

ctx.x: Well, now, when you play High Society, I know you play that part that everybody plays, and then you go home and play another variation. Where did you get that second variation from? Well, it's just my own idea. I just make anything up to my mind. Mm-hmm. Well, that's a very nice solo. I've always liked that through the years.

I think that's a good one. There's another number. I know there's a special kind of featured Kranath part. That's St. Louis Blues. I know you and Piku, Rie Lee Barnes, George Lewis, all play that one special little part, you know, that chorus. That you mean that solo? Yeah.

Well, that's a, that solo, that's been, that was on orchestration. That's the first, that's the first solo I learned to play in St. Louis Blues. Of course, I makes it a little different from because it was, you know, I could brush it up a little, but most of it is just, it was, that was written. It was written. Do you remember the first time you saw it? It was an orchestration, and all of, all of the time they played, they made that. That's when you go real high. Yeah. Well, you read it off the orchestration…
